title: Australia Student Visa Changes Split Families and Force Offshore Applications
excerpt: Rules in force since 2 October 2026 bar most students from including family, abolish adding family after grant with no exemptions, and push further applications offshore — leaving students whose visas expire mid-course, and families planning to reunite, with hard deadlines.
body:
• Since 2 October 2026, most international students in Australia can no longer include a partner or children in a Student visa (subclass 500) application, and no student visa holder can add family after the visa is granted — Home Affairs states there are no exemptions to that second rule.
  • Family can still be included at application only in exempt cases: PhD students, DFAT or Defence-sponsored students, foreign government scholarship recipients, and eligible students from Pacific and ASEAN countries — a list that does not cover most Indian students, who qualify only through the PhD, sponsorship or scholarship exemptions.
  • Most temporary visa holders, including current students seeking a further visa, must now be outside Australia when they lodge and when it is granted, unless an exemption applies; applications lodged before 2 October 2026 keep the old rules.
  • Decide on family before you lodge: exempt families must apply together, at the same time and in the same location as the student — family cannot be added later in any circumstance.

Fatima Bonna memorised her student visa conditions when she began studying in Adelaide last year. Then the rules changed underneath her. Bonna, 27, from Bangladesh, is studying a master's in early childhood education at the Ikon Institute; her visa expires next September, four months before her course finishes, and under Australia's new rules she will be required to travel offshore to apply for a new one. "I can't sleep at night," she told The Guardian.

Who is affected — exactly

The changes apply to Student visa (subclass 500) and Student Guardian visa (subclass 590) applicants and took effect on 2 October 2026. They hit students who hoped to bring a partner or children, current holders who planned to add family later or lodge a further visa onshore, and temporary visa holders planning to switch into study. Current visas are unaffected, and applications lodged before 2 October 2026 are assessed under the old rules, the Law Council of Australia says.

What changed, precisely

First, family. Student visa applicants can no longer include family members unless an exemption applies, and this applies to a first or a further Student visa alike. The Department of Home Affairs page on including or adding family members lists the exemptions as PhD students, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Defence-sponsored students, foreign government scholarship recipients, and eligible students from Pacific countries and ASEAN member countries, with narrow continuity cases for family already on a current Student visa. Included family must be in the same location as the student at lodgement. And no one can add family afterwards: "Current Student visa holders are no longer able to add family members after their Student visa has been granted. There are no exemptions to this rule," Home Affairs states.

That second point upended Wina Satria's plans. Satria, a PhD candidate from Indonesia at the University of Sydney, arrived last year with her then two-year-old son and planned to add her husband next year to help raise the child. Even as a PhD student — exempt at application — she cannot add a relative to a visa already granted. "I was shocked," she told The Guardian. "It's hard if we can't have our family with us." Assistant Minister Julian Hill said the government was "not in the business of separating families already onshore in Australia," The Guardian reported.

Second, place of application. Most temporary visa holders in Australia must now be outside Australia when they lodge a Student or Student Guardian application and when it is granted, and the rule also affects current Student visa holders applying for another Student visa unless an exemption applies — exemptions include needing additional time to complete a course, provider default, specific cohorts and certain course progressions, according to the Law Council of Australia's publication of the Home Affairs advice. Melbourne agent Gurpreet Dhawan told The Guardian the offshore requirement can leave students in limbo: "It's a huge risk." The Guardian reported, citing Home Affairs, that about 50 percent of higher education applications are processed within 16 days, and 90 percent within four months.

Why the government did it — and the wider warning

The Albanese government says the changes target "visa hopping" and are designed to help bring net overseas migration down from almost 300,000 a year to 225,000 by mid-2028, The Guardian reported. The university sector's warning is broader. Bill Shorten, the former Labor minister now vice-chancellor of the University of Canberra, told The Saturday Paper the tinkering has to stop: "Many universities are precariously financed. The sector is financed by increasing student debt and by overseas students." Monash professor Andrew Norton says institutions attracting higher proportions of students from South Asia are likely to take the brunt, The Saturday Paper reported.

What to do next — and what happens if you do nothing

Check whether an exemption covers you on the Home Affairs family members page and the subclass 500 guidance it links to. If you are exempt and want your family with you, they must be in the application, in the same location, at lodgement — there is no later route. If your visa expires before your course ends, plan the offshore application and processing window into your study calendar. Doing nothing is not neutral: lodging onshore without an exemption, or deferring a partner's arrival until after grant, has no fallback — the family decision cannot be revisited once the visa is granted.

nri_angle: India is neither a Pacific nor an ASEAN country, so most Indian students in Australia can include family only via the PhD, DFAT/Defence sponsorship or fully funded foreign government scholarship exemptions — and with onshore applications largely closed and family additions after grant abolished, Indian families must settle study, spouse and childcare plans before the first application is lodged.
